Ghetto Blaster
GET-oh BLAS-ter
noun (Gen X slang)
A late-1970s and 1980s name, in America and Britain, for the large portable radio-cassette player also called the boombox. Ghetto comes from Venice, where in 1516 the city confined its Jews to a quarter called the Ghetto, probably from the Venetian word for the foundry that had stood there; it later named Jewish quarters across Europe, the walled ghettos of the Nazi era, and in 20th-century America the segregated, poor city neighborhoods where many Black and Puerto Rican families lived. Blaster is one who blasts, here at full volume. The compound tied the loud radio to the young people of those neighborhoods, and from the start it carried a racial edge; in Britain it was often used without that awareness. Most Americans now say boombox.

Biblical Definition

Ghetto blaster was a common 1980s name for the boombox, and many people said it without a second thought. But the word deserves one. Ghetto has a long and painful history: the walled quarter where Venice shut in its Jews, the ghettos where the Nazis starved them, and the segregated American neighborhoods where Black and Puerto Rican families were hemmed in by law, lending, and prejudice. To call a loud radio a ghetto blaster was to attach it to the young people of those streets, and often to sneer at them for being loud. The Christian observation is that Scripture gives no room for that sneer. God "hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth" (Act 17:26). James forbids holding the faith of Christ "with respect of persons" (Jas 2:1). In Christ "There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free… for ye are all one in Christ Jesus" (Gal 3:28), and heaven’s choir is "a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues" (Rev 7:9). The men and women who first carried those radios gave America breakdancing and hip-hop, and they are image-bearers before they are anything else. Words matter: "Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt" (Col 4:6). A father can explain the old term honestly to his children, tell them where ghetto came from, and teach them to say boombox instead — not out of fear, but because a Christian chooses words that honor his neighbor.

Webster 1828 Definition

1980s name for the boombox that tied the loud radio to the poor Black and Latino neighborhoods called ghettos, a word with a long history of segregation; Scripture makes all nations of one blood (Act 17:26) and forbids respect of persons (Jas 2:1).

GHETTO BLASTER, n. (Gen X slang, late 1970s–1980s, US and UK) A large portable radio-cassette player; a boombox. "Somebody had a ghetto blaster on the bleachers."

Ghetto, from Venice (1516), first the Jewish quarter, later any segregated poor district; blaster, one who plays music at full blast.

The term carries a racial edge, associating loud music with Black and Latino urban youth; the preferred word is boombox.

No entry in Webster 1828; the compound is late-20th-century slang.

Decode for parents: explain the history of ghetto honestly and teach your children to choose the word that honors their neighbor.

Key Scripture

Act 17:26 — "And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;"

Jas 2:1 — "My brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons."

Gal 3:28 — "There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus."

Rev 7:9 — "After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues, stood before the throne, and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, and palms in their hands;"

Col 4:6 — "Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man."

Modern Corruption

Ghetto blaster named a radio by the neighborhoods of the poor and segregated, often as a sneer; Scripture makes all nations of one blood and asks a Christian to choose words that honor his neighbor.

expand to see more

A word with a wall around it. Ghetto began as a place where a city walled in people it despised, and in America it came to mean neighborhoods shaped by segregation and poverty. Naming a loud radio after those streets quietly blamed their young people for the noise and treated their culture as a nuisance. That is respect of persons, which James forbids to anyone who holds the faith of the Lord of glory (Jas 2:1). God made every nation of one blood (Act 17:26); no neighborhood is beneath His notice.

Speech seasoned with salt. Many who said ghetto blaster in 1984 meant nothing by it, and a father need not accuse them. But Christians are told to let their speech be always with grace (Col 4:6), and grace notices how a word lands. The boombox culture of New York gave the world music and dance it still enjoys. Heaven will be full of every kindred and tongue (Rev 7:9); it is good practice to speak of them now as we will stand beside them then.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Venetian Ghetto (1516, the Jewish quarter) → European and Nazi-era ghettos → 20th-century US segregated neighborhoods → ghetto blaster (late 1970s–80s) → boombox preferred; Scripture: of one blood all nations (Act 17:26).

expand to see more

1516 Venice: the Ghetto, the quarter where Jews were confined; probably from Venetian getto, foundry

Later Jewish quarters across Europe; the walled ghettos of the Nazi era

20th-century America: segregated, poor urban neighborhoods, especially Black and Puerto Rican

Late 1970s–1980s: ghetto blaster for the boombox; racial edge noted, boombox preferred

Biblical answer: one blood (Act 17:26); no respect of persons (Jas 2:1); every kindred and tongue (Rev 7:9)

Usage

""Dad, why did they call it a ghetto blaster?""

"Have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ… with respect of persons (Jas 2:1)."

"Let your speech be alway with grace (Col 4:6) — call it a boombox."
